text:
alex: Heads-up — we need to finalize the backpressure / saturation signals for the new batching dashboard. Runtime + infra inputs required for console panels and alerting. Can we align on metric names, cardinality, and SLO-ish thresholds? cc @maria @sam @priya :eyes:
maria: +1. do you have a concrete list of signals you want displayed vs what runtime can emit?
sam: Runtime can emit these today (rough sketches):
- batch_size_distribution (histogram)
- batch_wait_seconds (histogram + quantiles)
- active_slots (gauge)
- queue_depth (gauge)
- saturation_events_total (counter for when dispatch queue is > capacity threshold)
- headroom_percentage (gauge derived at scrape time)
We use these prom names: `redwood_batch_size_bucket`, `redwood_batch_wait_seconds_bucket`, `redwood_active_slots`, `redwood_queue_depth`, `redwood_saturation_events_total`, `redwood_headroom_pct`.
priya: For console we want: time-series of p50/p95/p99 wait, evolving batch size CDF, a heatmap of saturation by region, and a single saturation_score to power alerts. Can runtime produce a single normalized score?
sam: We can emit a `redwood_saturation_score` gauge (0-1) computed per dispatcher: formula roughly `min(1, (queue_depth / queue_capacity) * (1 + recent_fill_rate_multiplier))`. But note we don't want very high cardinality. Suggest by-region and by-tier only.
jin: cardinality note — avoid per-model/per-route tags for the saturation_score metric. That would explode series during spikes. Keep labels: region, pool_type (dedicated/shared), tier (prod/canary).
alex: Good call. Priya, console expects per-route drilldown though. How do we reconcile?
priya: We can show per-route insights by sampling or by joining lower-cardinality metrics with request logs in the console backend. For the default dashboard we only surface low-cardinality signals and add a 'route detail' panel that queries the logs/trace index on demand.
sam: Also suggests a lightweight rolling histogram for batch_size to compute percentiles server-side and expose p10/50/90/99 as gauges: `redwood_batch_size_pXX`. That reduces cost vs raw histogram for long retention.
maria: For alerting, propose two signals:
- saturation_score >= 0.85 sustained for 5m -> page oncall
- p99 batch wait > 250ms for 3m -> page
Both with sensible throttles. Thoughts?
jin: +1 on thresholds but infra will also need `queue_capacity` metric to sanity-check headroom calc. Add `redwood_queue_capacity` gauge.
console-bot: deploybot: new metrics schema PR opened: https://git.redwood/inframetrics/pull/432 — includes `redwood_saturation_score` + headroom change set. CI shows no cardinality regression in staging.
alex: Next actions:
- sam: add `redwood_saturation_score` (labels: region,pool_type,tier) + `redwood_queue_capacity` -> due EOD Thu (1726080000)
- jin: run a cardinality stress job on the staging scrape for 24h and share numbers -> due Mon
- priya: prototype dashboard panels (low-cardinality view + drilldown flow) and share mock -> due Tue
- maria: draft alert runbook w/ thresholds and expected mitigation steps -> due Tue

Anyone object to that split? :+1: / -1:
maria: +1
sam: +1
priya: +1
jin: +1
alex: Awesome. I'll follow-up with the console schema and a short notes PR for the runbook.
